'''Desmond MacHale''' (born 28 January 1946) is an Irish [[Mathematics|mathematician]] who is Emeritus [[Professor]] of Mathematics at [[University College Cork]].<ref name=boole/><ref>{{cite news|title=How Dev was nearly lost to science|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sciencetoday/2010/0513/1224270275922.html|accessdate=4 January 2011|newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]|date=13 May 2010}}</ref> He is an author and speaker on several subjects, including [[George Boole]], lateral thinking puzzles, and humour.  He has published over 80 books, some of which have been translated into languages including Danish, Italian, Norwegian, Spanish, German, Korean, and Japanese.<ref>{{cite news|title=Amazon, Books by Des MacHale|url=https://www.amazon.co.uk/Des-MacHale/e/B001IXMKYW/ref=dp_byline_cont_book_1/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Mercier Press, Authors, Des MacHale|url=http://www.mercierpress.ie/authors/desmachale/}}</ref>

==Biography==
Des MacHale was born in [[Castlebar]], County Mayo.  He earned his BSc and MSc in mathematical science at [[University of Galway|University College Galway]] in 1967 and 1968, and completed his PhD at the [[Keele University|University of Keele]] in 1972 under Hans Liebeck.  Since then he has been at [[University College Cork]], where his research has focussed on [[group theory|group]] and [[ring theory]], especially [[Boolean rings]].<ref name=boole>[http://georgeboole.com/film/documentary/machale/ Celebrating George Boole's Bicentenary: Professor Desmond MacHale]</ref>

In 1985 MacHale published ''George Boole: His Life and Work'', the first book length biography of Boole.<ref name=new&views>[https://www.ucc.ie/en/conferrings/honorary/archive/dr-desmond-machale-degree-of-doctor-of-literature.html UCC to honour education stars: Desmond MacHale]</ref> In 2014, a year ahead of Boole's bicentennial, this was reissued in revised and expanded form as ''The Life and Work of George Boole: A Prelude to the Digital Age''. He is considered the world's leading expert on Boole and in 2018 published another book ''New Light on George Boole'', co-authored with Yvonne Cohen.<ref>''[http://www.mathsireland.ie/blog/2016_11_cm Des MacHale: The Best Friend George Boole Ever Had]'' Annals of Irish Mathematics</ref><ref name=award/>

MacHale has also authored books on other subjects, including brainteasers and he has written more than 30 books of jokes and discussions of humour.<ref>''[https://www.independent.co.uk/news/why-did-the-irishman-break-the-rules-1365723.html Why did the Irishman break the rules?]'' by Paul Vallely, The Independent Online, 29 September 1996</ref> His ''Comic Sections: The Book of Mathematical Jokes, Humour, Wit and Wisdom'' is a book which combines two of his interests. He has written over a dozen books of [[lateral thinking]] problems with author [[Paul Sloane (speaker)|Paul Sloane]]; and many of these problems are featured on the [[Futility Closet]] website.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kohler|first=Chris|title=Hands On: Sloane and MacHale, New DS Puzzler From Layton Developer|url=https://www.wired.com/gamelife/2009/06/sloane-machale|accessdate=4 January 2011|newspaper=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]}}</ref> He has written several books about the 1952 American film, ''[[The Quiet Man]]''. He has spoken at schools, on radio, and television on the subjects of mathematics, humour, and puzzles.<ref>{{cite news|title=Youtube: Des MacHale on humour and puzzles|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HdpMywvX4UQ/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/HdpMywvX4UQ |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

MacHale designed the logo of the [[Irish Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.irishmathsoc.org/news05/M0501.pdf Mathematical Society News] Logo design by Des MacHale</ref>

He is a longtime opponent of smoking, and for decades has played a role within the Irish Association of Non-Smokers. He appeared on [[RTÉ]]'s ''[[The Late Late Show (Irish talk show)|The Late Late Show]]'' as early as the 1980s in an attempt to educate the public about the dangers of smoking.<ref name=new&views/>

His son [[Dominic MacHale]] is an actor, known for [[The Young Offenders (film)|The Young Offenders]].<ref name="Echo Live">{{cite web | title=On The Buses: Public transport gets CCCahoots treatment | website=Echo Live | date=16 January 2019 | url=https://www.echolive.ie/corknews/On-The-Buses-Public-transport-gets-CCCahoots-treatment-591a95f2-c008-4e2f-9258-73921f111b61-ds | access-date=2019-11-06}}</ref><ref name="Fitzpatrick 2019">{{cite web | last=Fitzpatrick | first=Pat | title=Made in Munster: 'I was down to a euro' - Watch The Young Offenders actors tell of struggle to make it in acting | website=Irish Examiner | date=2019-10-22 | url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/lifestyle/features/made-in-munster-i-was-down-to-a-euro--watch-the-young-offenders-actors-tell-of-struggle-to-make-it-in-acting-956992.html | access-date=2019-11-06}}</ref>

==Superbrain competition==
From 1984 to 2007, MacHale ran the Superbrain Competition at [[University College Cork]], including setting the questions and grading the papers.<ref>[https://www.ucc.ie/en/matsci/scholar-awards/#d.en.638168 Superbrain Winners] University College Cork: Mathematical Sciences Scholarships & Awards</ref> A book of the questions (with solutions) from 1984 to 2008 was published in 2011 as ''The First Twenty-Five Years of the Superbrain'' by Diarmuid Early & Des MacHale.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Leversha|first=Gerry|date=March 2011|title=Superbrain: the first twenty-five years, by Diarmuid Early and MacHale. Des Pp. 230. £13.00. 2009. {{text|ISBN}}: 978-1906338015 (HighPerception).|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/mathematical-gazette/article/superbrain-the-first-twentyfive-years-by-diarmuid-early-and-machale-des-pp-230-1300-2009-isbn-9781906338015-highperception/AD3DBA06DD4FDB595ADD03CA42C11783|journal=The Mathematical Gazette|language=en|volume=95|issue=532|pages=171–172|doi=10.1017/S0025557200007543|s2cid=183131270 |issn=0025-5572|via=|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
On George Boole Day, 2 November 2015, University College Cork awarded MacHale an honorary doctorate of literature in recognition of his contributions to scholarship on Boole.<ref>On receiving the award MacHale said, "The world has finally come to realise the genius of George Boole internationally and the United Nations' declaration this year was a major achievement. Everyone in the world now has heard about George Boole."</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20170115124755/https://www.ucc.ie/en/conferrings/honorary/archive/text-617702-en.html Honorary Conferrings Speeches Archive: Dr Desmond MacHale, Degree of Doctor of Literature] Address delivered by Professor [[John A. Murphy]]</ref>

On 15 October 2016 [[Maths Week Ireland]] presented MacHale with the inaugural "Raising Public Awareness of Maths" award.<ref name=award>[http://www.mathsweek.ie/2016/news/des-machale-1st-recipient-of-inaugural-maths-week-raising-public-awareness-of-maths-award Des Machale receives Public Awareness of Maths Award] 10th annual Maths Week Ireland</ref><ref>[https://www.siliconrepublic.com/discovery/des-machale-ucc-award-mobius-strip Irish mathematician Des MacHale honoured with Maths Week award] by Colm Gorey, Silicon Republic, 16 October 2016.</ref> In 2026, he was made a member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-22 |title=29 new members admitted to the Royal Irish Academy |url=https://www.ria.ie/2026/05/22/29-new-members-admitted-to-the-royal-irish-academy/ |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=Royal Irish Academy }}</ref>
